syllabusTopics: Gaseous state: Kinetic theory of gas and its postulates
Gas laws: Boyle's law, Charles' law, Avogadro's law, combined gas equation, Dalton's law of partial pressure, Graham's law of diffusion
Ideal gas and ideal gas equation; universal gas constant and its significance
Deviation of real gas from ideality (solving related numerical problems based on gas laws)
Liquid state: physical properties of liquids — evaporation and condensation, vapour pressure and boiling point, surface tension and viscosity (qualitative idea only)
Solid state: types of solids, amorphous and crystalline solids
Efflorescent, deliquescent and hygroscopic solids; crystallization and crystal growth; water of crystallization
Introduction to unit crystal lattice and unit cell

$$1\ \text{atm}=101325\ \text{Pa}=760\ \text{mm Hg}=1.01325\ \text{bar};\qquad T(\text{K})=t(\degree\text{C})+273.15$$
$$PV=\tfrac{1}{3}mn\bar{c}^{2},\qquad KE=\tfrac{3}{2}kT\ (\text{molecule})=\tfrac{3}{2}RT\ (\text{mole})$$
$$\text{idealisations: point molecules + no attraction}$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Gases have negligible mass. ✅ They have small but definite mass — 22.4 L of air weighs about 29 g at STP.  ·  ❌ Temperature in gas laws may be taken in °C. ✅ Absolute (kelvin) temperature only; 0 °C is 273.15 K.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Air is a mixture (78% N₂, 21% O₂, ~1% Ar/CO₂) that behaves nearly ideally at 1 atm — the everyday ideal gas.  ·  One mole of any gas at STP occupies 22.4 L and, for air, weighs ≈28.97 g (average molar mass).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Express 2.5 atm in mm Hg and Pa. **Solution:** 2.5 × 760 = 1900 mm Hg; 2.5 × 101325 = 253 312 Pa ≈ 2.53 × 10⁵ Pa.  ·  **Problem:** Which postulate fails when a gas is compressed to 200 atm? **Solution:** 'molecular volume is negligible' — the molecules' own volume is no longer negligible against the container volume, so the free space shrinks and observed pressure exceeds the ideal prediction (Z > 1).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ A gas exerts pressure only downward. ✅ Pressure is isotropic — equal in every direction.  ·  ❌ 'Negligible molecular volume' is a minor technicality. ✅ It is one of the two postulates whose failure defines all real-gas deviation (the other is no attraction).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: What defines a gas and the four measurable variables (P, V, T, n) whose relationships the gas laws and kinetic theory explain — the orientation before the postulates.  ·  ### Defining characteristics of the gaseous state

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: The mean free path at 1 atm is ≈10⁻⁷ m — molecules travel ~1000 diameters between collisions.  ·  Every postulate is an idealisation — the model is defined by what it ignores.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Fix the four variables (P, V, T, n) in mind before the laws — every law is a two-at-a-time relation among them.  ·  Use kelvin always; the °C slip is the classic numerical error.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The pressure equation was derived by Clausius (1857); Maxwell gave the speed distribution in 1860.  ·  The two failed idealisations reappear as the van der Waals constants b (volume) and a (attraction).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: In kinetic theory, the pressure of a gas is proportional to: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: • No fixed shape or volume — a gas fills its container completely.  ·  • Very low density compared with liquids/solids (air ≈ 1.3 kg m⁻³ vs water 1000 kg m⁻³); highly compressible; diffuse rapidly.  ·  • Molecules are far apart (intermolecular distances ≈ 10 molecular diameters at STP) with negligible attraction — hence expansion and compressibility.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Kinetic theory explains why gases liquefy. ✅ It cannot — liquefaction comes from the attractive forces it assumes away; that requires the van der Waals model.  ·  ❌ Elastic collisions mean molecules never exchange energy. ✅ They exchange freely but the *total* KE is conserved.  ·  Learn the postulates as a cause–effect chain; examiners award marks for linking postulate → law → limitation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Quote the two 'failure postulates' explicitly in any limitations answer.  ·  List the four measurable properties of a gas and their SI units.  ·  State three characteristics that distinguish gases from liquids and solids.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Convert 750 mm Hg into Pa and bar.  ·  Why do gases fill the entire container while liquids do not?  ·  State the postulates of the kinetic theory and identify the two idealisations responsible for real-gas deviation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Show how PV = (1/3)mnc̄² leads to PV = nRT.  ·  Map each gas law to the postulates that explain it.  ·  Why does the kinetic theory fail for polyatomic gases' specific heats?

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • Exerts pressure uniformly in all directions (momentum transfer on wall collisions).  ·  • Mixes completely and homogeneously (diffusion, effusion through pinholes).  ·  ### The four state variables
